people.story: Michell was two months old when I met her mum during 1961 Christmas holidays. I was working nights at Roe-Lee Mills while the college was on holidays. I got off night shift and went straight to bed until I was woken up by the cry of a baby esuing from my sitting room. I was living at number 40 London  road Blacburn. The whole three story building was occupied by students. I occupied the whole first floor comprising of bedroom, large sitting room, common dinning-room, common kitchen and a dual bathroom cum toilet. The other students have bedrooms only on the second and third floor. There was an attic-room which was rarely occupied because it was so cold. As far as mine memory serves me, all the students were from the CommonWealth which explains why the attic was rarely occupied. There was a birthday party at the weedend and Sandra was among the revelers. I am not sure wheather she was invited or she was just a gate crasher, Subsquent events led me to believe that she could only have been a gate crasher.

people.story:
My dearest beloved Omoyeni was married to my uncle Agbelayi of Igbemo. He died in his prime and my brother Samuel Olotu Ojo Rotimi inherited Omoyeni according to our custorm. This custorm is almost extinct which is a shame because it dates back to the days of Abraham whereby widows pass on to there nearest relative. Ruth, Naomi's daughter-in-law was a good example of how the custorm was. The children of the deceased are automatically provided with a father who loves and cares for them; almost and sometimes more than their real dead father.

I was told that Omoyeni gave me my first name some time after I was born. I was deliberately not given a name at birth because my parents were almost certain that I would not live given that they lost a few children before  me shortly after they were born.

I have a very  strong spiritual connection with Omoyeni. Forgive me for not including your name on the first list. I love you "Mum" Omoyeni. You have always been and feel like my mum. I will always love and cherish you my dearest beloved Omoyeni.

MARRIAGE: Maried to Adeleye of Ilaso. Her eldest is Abigail who later married my dad, David Ajayi Rotimi. There was an unspoken rivalry between her and my mum. the rivalry was always initiated by her. It was never encouraged or didcouraged by my mum, Adegbolarin Omoje Okangi.
